messages:
Ava (customer): Hey team — hitting what feels like throttling during bursts. Started around 10:20am UTC. Endpoint /v1/generate returns intermittent 429s, and when it doesn't 429 the tail latency jumps to 800-1200ms. We saw a spike in token usage and billing meter. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~85% to ~10% during the burst.

Maria: Sorry you're hitting this, Ava. Can you paste one or two X-Request-IDs (from response headers) and approximate time ranges? Also which model/route and whether you're on Hosted or Dedicated?

Ava (customer): Request IDs: req_20260320_01, req_20260320_07. Happened from 10:18:30 -> 10:22:00 UTC. Using hosted /v1/generate, model: rdx-large-4096, route: default-chat. We are single-tenant but using free-burst credits (not Dedicated). We also saw a bunch of queued requests in our app logs.

ops-bot: automated alert — quota.burst_exhaustion detected for project pid_88xx at 2026-03-20T10:19:12Z (metric: concurrent_tokens).

Lee: Thanks, digging in. Two things to watch: continuous batching can add a small wait to coalesce tokens — if there's a high-concurrency spike with lots of short requests we'll see batching latency + queueing. Also if KV cache warms get invalidated (prefix skew) the model does extra compute and batching windows align poorly -> perceived throttle.

Sam: Agreed. From infra side we've seen cases where KV prefetch misfires during big jittery bursts — hit rate collapses, backend does full decode more often, which increases GPU time and reduces throughput, triggering rate-limiters.

Maria: Quick repro request: can you run a short, deterministic burst while we watch? Example curl load (5 threads, 40 reqs each, small prompt):

```bash
for i in {1..40}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rdx-large-4096","input":"Hello","max_tokens":32}' &
done; wait
```

And capture response headers + timings: `curl -w "time_total:%{time_total} status:%{http_code} header:%{response_header}"`

Ava (customer): Running now, will attach logs in ~5m.

Lee: In parallel can you share your client SDK config? Specifically: batch_max_tokens, batch_max_latency_ms, kv_prefetch (true/false), and any custom backoff logic. If batch_max_latency_ms is high (e.g., 50ms) and your burst consists of many small requests spaced out, they'll wait to coalesce and you'll see queueing bursts.

Ava (customer): We're using the JS SDK defaults: batch_max_latency_ms=25, batch_max_tokens=2048, kv_prefetch=false (we haven't toggled).

Sam: That helps. Two tactical mitigations while we investigate: 1) Flip on kv_prefetch for hot prefixes (helps warm KV before requests land), 2) For latency-sensitive routes set batch_max_latency_ms=5 or enable prefer_low_latency routing so we sacrifice token-efficiency for lower tail latency. Also temporarily raise burst quota if you're on pay-as-you-go to avoid 429s while warming.

Maria: I'm opening a support escalation (SE-2319) and linking eng-runtime. Action items: Maria (support) — capture backend traces for req_20260320_01/07 and check per-route rate-limiter logs; Lee (infra) — verify KV cache eviction events + prefix affinity around 10:18-10:22; Sam (ml) — check that batching windows didn't increase due to skewed sequence lengths and confirm whether kernel selection fell back to slower path.

Lee: Quick snippet from runtime logs around 10:19 (sanitized):

```
[10:19:11] req=req_20260320_01 state=queued BATCH_WAIT_MS=124 kv_hit_rate=11% gpu_ms=220
[10:19:12] req=req_20260320_02 state=processing BATCH_SIZE=8 kv_hit_rate=12% gpu_ms=210
[10:19:13] rate_limiter: token_bucket_reject project=pid_88xx available_tokens=0
```

Lee: That matches the symptoms — long batch wait + low kv hit rate + token_bucket exhausted -> 429s.

Ava (customer): Ok interesting. Is there a recommended default kv_prefetch pattern? We have thousands of possible prompt prefixes, but a small hot set.

Sam: If you have a hot set, enable kv_prefetch on those prefixes and pre-warm with a low-rate background fanout (e.g., 1 req/s per prefix for a minute) before expected bursts. Also set prefix_affinity so requests with the same prefix land on warm shards. For ephemeral cold prefixes prefer shorter context or bump max_tokens lower to reduce GPU time.

Maria: Short-term: we're increasing your burst quota by +25% for the next hour while you run repros. Please also try Sam's low-latency SDK setting so we can confirm tail latency improves.

Ava (customer): Thanks. Running the curl burst now with batch_max_latency_ms=5 and kv_prefetch=true. Will paste headers and a micro-trace when done. :raised_hands:

ops-bot: ticket SE-2319 created and assigned to eng-runtime, eng-infra, se-team. Priority: P2.

Maria: Thanks everyone. If the repro shows improved tail latency we can recommend permanent config changes or help craft a pre-warm job. If not, we'll capture full traces and escalate to a kernel-level perf investigation.

Ava (customer): First pass looks better — avg time_total ~0.09s, few 429s. I'll keep testing and upload the full curl output to the ticket.

Maria: Perfect. Leaving this thread open until traces are confirmed and a persistent mitigation is applied. :white_check_mark:
